title: Financial freedom of Filipinos in personal finance management
tldr: Filipinos exhibit financial literacy challenges rooted in cultural attitudes, with cash, debt, risk, and wealth management dimensions showing efficiency but needing improvement.
problem_and_motivation: Most Filipinos lack financial awareness and do not understand the purpose of financial instruments for achieving true financial wellness. Cultural tendencies like the come-what-may attitude and reliance on traditional saving methods hinder effective budgeting, savings, and investment practices. There is a need to examine the degree of financial freedom across different personal finance dimensions.
approach: Employed descriptive methodology with survey questionnaires for 150 respondents.
Studied employees from ten major Philippine Stock Exchange Index corporations in Metro Manila.
Assessed four dimensions: cash management, debt management, risk management, and wealth management.
Used weighted mean and linear regression analysis to evaluate financial freedom degrees.
Collected demographic and work profile data including income levels and management positions.
findings: num: 57% of respondents are male, 63% married, 43% aged 31-40 years.
num: 40% earn ₱30,000 or above monthly, 50% have 11-18 years of work experience.
num: Cash management weighted mean of 3.73 indicates good practices needing improvement.
num: Debt management weighted mean of 3.70 shows agreement with effective strategies.
num: Cash, debt, risk, and wealth management do not significantly contribute to financial freedom.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This study examines the financial freedom dimensions of Filipino corporate employees across cash, debt, risk, and wealth management. It identifies cultural factors like the come-what-may attitude that hinder effective financial practices. The research demonstrates that these four dimensions do not significantly predict overall financial freedom. Findings highlight the need for comprehensive financial education addressing both knowledge and behavioral aspects.
directly_justifies: Filipinos exhibit traditional mindsets favoring physical savings over bank deposits.
Emergency fund preparedness is low leading to debt reliance during unexpected expenses.
Risk management through insurance is undervalued due to cultural perceptions.
Financial freedom requires integration of multiple personal finance practices.
limits: Limited to employees of ten major corporations in Metro Manila.
Cross-sectional design does not capture changes in financial behavior over time.
Self-reported data may suffer from social desirability and recall bias.
Does not account for external economic factors affecting financial decisions.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan of all topic domains identified high relevance for financial behavior (1.C), financial behavioral profiles (5.A), budgeting strategies (7.A), and culturally specific practices (2.A) as core themes. Medium relevance for Filipino young professionals (1.A), savings management (13.A), debt management (13.B), and evaluation frameworks (12.A) as supporting aspects. Low relevance for expense categorization (3.A), landscape of existing systems (4.A), and engagement dynamics (11.A) as contextual mentions. Domains related to predictive modeling, anomaly detection, and ML model serving were considered and rejected as not covered by this personal finance management study.
